title: Presbycusis
keyPoints: Bilateral, symmetrical, high-frequency first
Impaired speech discrimination especially in noise
Audiogram: sloping high-frequency loss
Treatment: hearing aids, cochlear implant if severe
Counsel communication strategies
clinicalContext: 72-y-old with progressive hearing loss worse in crowded rooms.
nursingPriority: Refer for pure-tone audiometry, hearing-aid assessment; counsel face-to-face communication, reduced background noise.

title: Otoscope examination
definition: Ear canal and tympanic membrane inspection.
keyPoints: Pull pinna up-back (adult), down-back (child <3 y)
Normal TM: pearly-grey, cone of light anteroinferior (5 o'clock right, 7 o'clock left)
AOM: red bulging TM; OME: retracted dull TM, fluid level
Pneumatic otoscopy: mobility assessment
nursingPriority: Pull pinna down-back for straightening canal, examine for red bulging TM, assess mobility with pneumatic otoscopy.

title: Laryngoscope
keyPoints: Indirect: mirror via oropharynx
Direct rigid: OT
Flexible fibreoptic: nasal route awake
Videolaryngoscope: intubation especially difficult airway
Blade types: Macintosh (curved), Miller (straight) — Miller for infants
nursingPriority: Use Miller 0 or 1 straight blade to lift epiglottis, visualize cords, 3.5-4.0 uncuffed ETT.

title: Acute epiglottitis
definition: H. influenzae type B (Hib) supraglottitis — pediatric emergency.
keyPoints: 4 Ds: Drooling, Dysphagia, Dysphonia, Distress
Tripod posture, muffled hot-potato voice, stridor
Lateral neck X-ray: thumb sign
Do NOT examine throat (laryngospasm risk); avoid distressing child
Airway: OT intubation by anesthetist, IV ceftriaxone
pearls: Hib vaccine has dramatically reduced incidence.
nursingPriority: Do NOT examine throat or put in supine; summon anesthetist for OT controlled intubation, IV ceftriaxone, keep child in mother's lap until intubated.

title: Meniere disease
keyPoints: Triad: vertigo + sensorineural hearing loss + tinnitus
Attacks last minutes to hours
Low-frequency hearing loss early
Treatment: low-salt diet, diuretics (hydrochlorothiazide), betahistine, intratympanic gentamicin for refractory
clinicalContext: 45-y-old with episodic vertigo, tinnitus, low-frequency hearing loss.
nursingPriority: Low-salt diet (<2 g/d), betahistine 16 mg TDS, prochlorperazine for acute attack, refer for audiometry.

title: Epistaxis — management
definition: Nose bleed from anterior (Little area, Kiesselbach plexus, 90%) or posterior (sphenopalatine artery).
keyPoints: First aid: lean forward, pinch cartilaginous nose 10-15 min, ice pack on bridge
Anterior: silver nitrate cautery, anterior nasal pack
Posterior: balloon (Foley) or posterior gauze pack + admit
Systemic: correct coagulopathy, transfuse if severe
Identify and treat underlying (HTN, coagulopathy)
pearls: Do NOT lean head back — aspiration risk.
clinicalContext: Adult with active anterior nose bleed.
nursingPriority: Sit upright leaning forward, pinch cartilaginous nose 10-15 min, ice on bridge; if persists, anterior pack with silver nitrate after vasoconstrictor (oxymetazoline).

title: Tinnitus
definition: Perception of sound without external stimulus.
keyPoints: Subjective (common) vs objective (vascular)
Causes: noise exposure, presbycusis, Meniere, drugs (aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, aspirin, quinine), acoustic neuroma
Treatment: masking, tinnitus retraining therapy, CBT; treat underlying
clinicalContext: Patient on furosemide with new tinnitus.
nursingPriority: Review dose (furosemide ototoxicity especially IV bolus), slow infusion, audiology referral.

title: Profound hearing loss
keyPoints: Classification: mild 26-40, moderate 41-55, mod-severe 56-70, severe 71-90, profound >90 dB
Causes: genetic (Connexin 26), TORCH, ototoxicity, trauma, noise
Rehabilitation: cochlear implant, sign language, lip reading
nursingPriority: Refer for BERA; if profound SNHL, evaluate for cochlear implantation (best outcome before 3 y).

title: Rinne and Weber tests
definition: Tuning-fork tests 512 Hz for hearing loss differentiation.
keyPoints: Rinne: AC vs BC at mastoid; normal AC>BC (positive)
Conductive loss: BC>AC (negative Rinne) on affected side
SN loss: AC>BC but reduced overall (positive Rinne but soft)
Weber: vibrating fork midline forehead
Conductive loss lateralizes to affected ear; SN loss lateralizes to normal ear
clinicalContext: Weber lateralizes right, Rinne negative right (BC>AC).
nursingPriority: Interpret: right conductive hearing loss; ENT referral, otoscopy, audiometry.
